result_text:
I changed the two mock-folder rules in `ScopingConventions.java` so any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` counts as test code. The existing scoping and convention tests in `codeanalyzer` pass. I didn't add a test for the new cases (`mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`), so they haven't been run through the real matcher.

The old patterns only allowed ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` and space after `mock`, and needed at least one such character. The new ones are `.*/__mock[^/\\]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/\\]*/.*`. The rest of the name can be anything except a path separator, so a plain `mock` folder, punctuation and non-ASCII characters all match, at any depth. The existing path matching already tries a slash-normalized form of the path, so Windows-style paths with backslashes also match.

The match can't cross a folder boundary. `remock/`, `demo/` and `src/main/java/` don't match, and neither do files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java`, because there the name isn't followed by a `/`. The old names (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`) all still fit the new pattern.
